# Session Recorder

> Session Recorder is a free, open-source, local-first Chrome extension for
> recording web bugs for AI coding agents. It captures clicks, console errors,
> network requests and responses, screenshots, video, voice narration, DOM
> interactions, annotations, and uploaded files, then exports an LLM-ready
> Markdown report for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, and other coding
> agents.

Key facts: no account, no backend, no telemetry. Recordings are stored in the
browser's IndexedDB and exported as a zip the user saves. Secrets (passwords,
authorization headers, token-like fields) are masked at capture time. Export is
token-budgeted at four levels — Full, Standard, Compact (~50k tokens), Minimal
(~15k tokens) — each with a live token estimate, and trimming is deterministic
with no model call. Manifest V3. Free software under the AGPL-3.0, developed
by Mohsen Azimi.

## Product

- [Overview](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/): what it captures, how the loop works, install.
- [Chrome Web Store listing](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/session-recorder/dboiheheijgmfpfhbmjggiijpgondghh): install the extension.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/mohsen1/session-recorder-chrome-extension): full source, architecture notes, report format spec. Licensed AGPL-3.0.
- [Privacy policy](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/privacy.html): what is stored, what never leaves the machine.

## Agent workflows

- [With Claude Code](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/claude-code/): unzip the report into the repo and prompt Claude Code against it.
- [With Cursor](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/cursor/): attach report.md to Cursor's Agent; includes a reusable project rule.
- [With Codex](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/codex/): local CLI and cloud-task workflows, plus an AGENTS.md snippet.
- [With ChatGPT](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/chatgpt/): upload one self-contained report instead of pasting screenshots.

## Reference

- [Example report](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/example-report/): a complete, sanitized report.md and the same request rendered at all four verbosity levels.
- [Bug reports AI coding agents can fix](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/ai-bug-report/): the eight signals a browser bug report needs, temporal ordering, token budgets, deterministic trimming vs AI summarization, redaction, and live-browser vs recorded evidence.
- [Local-first design](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/local-first/): what no-account/no-backend means in practice, and the trade-offs it costs.
- [Session Recorder vs Jam](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/jam-alternative/): factual comparison, including where Jam is the better choice.

- [Browser bug report template](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/bug-report-template/): copyable Markdown template, filled example, and a prompt for handing evidence to a coding agent.
